geometry_edits.rationale: Open the split as a true public seam instead of reconnecting it too early.
Increase the void between wings to improve publicness and reduce object-like enclosure.
Reduce the bulk of the split mass so the hierarchy reads as main volume plus support/void.
Bind the threshold cut to the verified access side.
Enlarge the entrance notch so the ground plane reads as publicly occupied and not merely clipped.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact mass in all four views, but it is closer to a faceted object than a neighborhood-living building. The parcel is contained, yet the visible dominant gesture is inward and sealed rather than outwardly public. There is a notch-like subtraction and some sectional relief, but the access edge does not resolve into a clearly legible public court, seam, or threshold aligned to the verified frontage. The form also feels somewhat over-faceted and sculptural for the brief, with only modest hierarchy between main volume and carved support pieces. It resonates with the supplied neighborhood references in its low-rise, courtyard-adjacent language, but it does not yet translate that principle into an explicit active ground condition or a stronger public void.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Clear low-rise massing with a carved central void and a legible bridge/upper connector can support neighborhood program well.
Campus-like grouping around a courtyard and stepped low-rise hierarchy can create active shared open space.
Elongated low-rise mass with a central atrium/courtyard and strong horizontal spread is useful for neighborhood-commercial hybrids.
Terraced, multi-wing composition with bridging elements and a central void supports public circulation and layered access.
Interlocking volumes with a large courtyard and voids under elevated blocks can produce a clear active threshold.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but the access response is weak relative to the verified road edge.
The mass is coherent in aggregate, but the street-facing threshold remains semantically underdeveloped.
Geometry summary suggests a notch and split-wing lineage, yet the result still reads as a mostly enclosed object rather than an active neighborhood edge.
